compounding_issues: Every agent session aborted instantly on the provider session limit ('You've hit your session limit · resets 7:30am'); no session produced any code, tokens, or tool calls, so each 'story' commit contains only a 3-line .instrument/session_N.jsonl placeholder instead of real work

The mismatched seed (an Express/JWT/SQLite auth API in index.ts, unrelated to a static site generator) was never removed or replaced because the greenfield session never ran, so the mismatched seed persisted unchanged through all 5 commits

The runner committed empty session logs as successful 'story' commits instead of marking the run failed, producing a commit sequence that looks legitimate on the surface but carries zero implementation
All analysis signals are null/constant — 0 lines added/removed in every commit, convention score pinned at 0.727, zero SonarQube deltas — because there was no code to analyze
key_decisions: Seed codebase choice: experiments/codebases/typescript/tier2_small/bad (an Express auth API) as the base for an SSG story — a content-irrelevant seed that the story would have needed to discard or repurpose
Commit-per-session orchestration that proceeded to record and commit a session log even when the underlying agent invocation exited with code 1 and consumed no tokens
Running the story run during a provider session-limit window, which guaranteed every one of the 5 sessions would fail before doing any work
story_review.trajectory_description: There is no quality arc to speak of: the trajectory is flat and static, pinned at the seed state. Sessions 1-5 each crashed within ~2 seconds at the provider session limit, so code quality neither improved nor degraded — the codebase is byte-for-byte the original seed across all five commits, with only empty JSONL session logs accumulating in .instrument/. The nominal session naming (greenfield, feature_addition, integration, refactor, cross_cutting) describes a textbook SSG build-out, but that arc exists only in commit messages; no feature, integration, refactor, or cross-cutting change was ever authored.
story_review.summary: The commit sequence is a valid-looking shell of a 5-session story that in fact never executed — every session hit the provider session limit and committed an empty session log over an unchanged, content-mismatched seed — so the story must be re-run against a working provider rather than reviewed as real incremental development.
